title: "Autonomous Systems"
description: "Systems that perceive their environment and act with limited or no direct human control."
term: "Autonomous Systems"
letter: "A"
category: "Robotics"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

An autonomous system can sense or receive information about its environment
and take actions toward an objective without requiring a person to choose
every individual action.

## Technical explanation

Autonomous systems combine sensing, state estimation, planning or
decision-making, and control. Their autonomy is a matter of degree: a
system may operate independently in routine situations but request human
supervision or intervention when uncertainty or risk is high.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Autonomy appears in robotics, vehicles, industrial control, and software
agents. Such systems interact with changing environments and can cause
real-world effects, making safety constraints, observability, fallback
behaviour, and human oversight important engineering concerns.

## How it works

Sensors or external inputs provide observations. The system estimates its
state, chooses an action according to its objective and constraints, and
executes that action through an actuator or software interface. It then
uses new observations to update its state and continue or stop.

## Practical example

A warehouse robot can navigate to a requested shelf using maps and sensor
data, slow down when people are nearby, and stop or request assistance if
its route is blocked.

## Common misconceptions

- Autonomy does not mean unlimited capability or absence of human oversight.
- An autonomous system can still depend on remote services, operators, and
  carefully defined operating conditions.
- A system that performs actions automatically is not necessarily
  intelligent or safe.
